brief: AI-growth optimism gave way to an AI funding-cost debate on GS's trading floor. Scrutiny of AI financing models, CoreWeave-related commentary and frontier-lab economics widened AI-related credit spreads to the year's worst levels and erased the AI leaders-vs-laggards basket's H1 2026 gains. GS's credit team calls neocloud and frontier-lab bonds the epicentre, but says the secular AI thesis stays intact as growth and funding needs reprice more realistically. OpenAI's CFO saying she should have bought more compute is cited as evidence of robust demand. This triggered a positioning unwind: VIX futures volume hit 3.6x normal, CBOE put volume set an all-time record, US long/short net leverage fell 3.2 points (the largest weekly drop since Liberation Day), and Global Tech posted its largest net selling since 2016, though managers added shorts over cutting longs. The Nasdaq had its worst week since Liberation Day and semiconductors their longest losing streak since 2008, de-rating from 29x to 17x earnings. GS calls this rotation, not capitulation: SPX ex-AI is outperforming, quality factors hit new highs, breadth improved, and positioning and sentiment are near washed-out levels. With 14% of the S&P reporting this week and 44% next, GS says earnings confirmation decides the next move.
